authority: Chief Electrical Inspector / State Electrical Inspectorate

description.en: An Electrical Contractor License is required for any person or firm undertaking electrical installation, maintenance, or repair work in India. The license is issued by the State Electrical Inspectorate under the provisions of the Indian Electricity Act, 2003 and the Central Electricity Authority (Measures relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations. The license ensures that electrical work is carried out by qualified and competent persons to prevent electrical accidents and ensure public safety.

verifiedConditions.claim: The applicant or the competent person employed by the applicant must hold a recognised qualification in electrical engineering — Diploma in Electrical Engineering, B.E./B.Tech in Electrical Engineering, ITI Electrician/Wireman certificate, or equivalent qualification recognised by the state electrical inspectorate.

The applicant or competent person must have practical experience in electrical installation work. The required experience period varies by qualification — typically 1-3 years for degree holders and 2-5 years for diploma/ITI holders, depending on the state and license category.

unverifiedEligibility: License categories and eligibility criteria vary by state. Some states have multiple categories (A, B, C) based on the voltage and capacity of electrical work permitted.
Some states may require the applicant to pass a competency test or examination.
Firms and companies must designate a qualified competent person who holds the required qualifications.
Renewal requirements may differ from initial license requirements.

requirements.claim: Prescribed application form from the state electrical inspectorate. Many states now offer online application through their respective electrical inspectorate portals.

Attested copies of educational qualification certificates — Diploma/Degree in Electrical Engineering, ITI Wireman/Electrician certificate, or equivalent recognised qualification. Mark sheets and passing certificates are required.
Experience certificates from licensed electrical contractors or recognised organisations where the applicant has worked, specifying the nature and duration of electrical installation work performed.
Identity proof (Aadhaar card, PAN card, passport, or voter ID) and address proof of the applicant.
Recent passport-size photographs of the applicant (typically 2-4 copies).
Payment receipt for the prescribed license fee. Fees vary by state and license category.

processInformation.claim: Submit the application form with all required documents and fee to the office of the Electrical Inspector or through the state's online portal. The application is registered and acknowledged.
The Electrical Inspectorate verifies the qualifications, experience certificates, and other documents submitted. Some states may conduct an interview or competency test.

Upon successful verification, the Electrical Inspector issues the contractor license specifying the category, permitted scope of work (voltage and capacity limits), validity period, and conditions. The license is typically valid for 3-5 years depending on the state.

output.claim: An Electrical Contractor License issued by the State Electrical Inspectorate authorising the holder to carry out electrical installation, maintenance, and repair work within the specified category and voltage limits. The license must be displayed at the contractor's place of business and produced on demand during inspections.

fees.claim: License fee varies by state and category. New license fees typically range from Rs. 500 to Rs. 5,000. Higher categories permitting work on higher voltages attract higher fees. Renewal fees are generally lower than new license fees.

processingTime.applicability: Electrical contractor license from application to issuance
processingTime.claim: Processing time varies by state. States with online systems may process applications within 15-21 days. States with manual processes may take 30-45 days. Some states have time-bound service delivery guarantees.

sources.title: Central Electricity Authority — Safety Regulations
sources.publisher: Central Electricity Authority, Ministry of Power, Government of India
sources.evidenceExcerpt: The CEA frames regulations for safety and electric supply under the Electricity Act, 2003. The CEA (Measures relating to Safety and Electric Supply) Regulations prescribe that electrical installation work must be carried out by licensed contractors. State Electrical Inspectorates implement these regulations and issue contractor licenses.
claimsSupported: Electrical contractor license is mandatory for carrying out electrical installation work.
The license is issued by the State Electrical Inspectorate.
Qualifications and experience requirements are prescribed by CEA regulations.
License categories define the scope of permitted work.
sources.uncertainty: State-specific rules, fee schedules, and license categories vary. Some states have additional requirements beyond CEA regulations.

limitations: This record provides a general overview. Specific license categories, fees, qualifications, and processes vary by state.
The record does not cover supervisor licenses (electrical supervisor/wireman licenses) which are different from contractor licenses.
Competency test or examination requirements vary by state and are not detailed.
The record does not cover licenses for specialised electrical work (lifts, escalators, high-voltage installations).
Renewal procedures and continuing education requirements are not covered in detail.

review.reviewReason: Central framework under CEA regulations is documented. State-specific implementation details need verification.
